SCENE CONTEXT — EXACTLY 2 PEOPLE. A dirt farm road at night. A man stands ON THE DIRT ROAD, ON THE
GROUND, BEHIND his own dead truck, with both boots in the dirt. He is facing up the road at a cold

<<<55a2272c-c687-4ec7-b2d9-c4c034da07dc>>>: TYLER — TRUCKER CAP with the brim

<<<00e57422-9dab-43de-aea3-9e73d4347c2d>>>: the pickup exterior — dead, doors open,

<<<e2d034de-3176-484a-9d6b-1697f783f53a>>>: the dirt road and corn walls — for GROUND
SURFACE and CORN only.

DO NOT use any reference to add a craft, a hull, a beam, or a third person. None of those appear.

⚠⚠ GROUND POSITION — READ THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE ⚠⚠

DANNY IS STANDING ON THE DIRT ROAD. BOTH BOOTS ARE ON THE GROUND, IN THE DIRT, AT ROAD LEVEL. His
full body weight is carried by the road surface.

HE IS NOT ON THE TRUCK. He is not standing on the tailgate, not standing in the truck bed, not on the

vehicle at any point in this clip. NO PART OF HIM IS EVER ABOVE ROAD LEVEL.

HE IS BEHIND THE TRUCK — a few feet back from its rear end, out in the open road, with the whole
vehicle in front of him.

HOW TO CHECK IT IN THE FRAME: THE TOP EDGE OF THE TRUCK BED CROSSES THE FRAME AT ROUGHLY HIS CHEST.
The truck's body and bed sit LOWER IN FRAME than his head and shoulders and OVERLAP HIS BODY FROM THE
CHEST DOWN. His head, shoulders and upper chest are above the bed line; his waist, hips and legs are
behind and below it. HIS FEET ARE NOT VISIBLE ABOVE THE TRUCK — they are on the road behind it.

HIS HAND RESTS ON THE TOP EDGE OF THE TAILGATE AT CHEST HEIGHT, reaching slightly forward and down to
do it. That reach is only possible because he is standing on the ground.

DIRT UNDER HIS BOOTS. Loose road dust around them, scuffed where he has been shifting his weight. His
shadow is thrown along the ROAD SURFACE, at road level, running toward and past the camera.

⚠⚠ THE SECOND INSTRUCTION THAT MATTERS MOST ⚠⚠

DANNY'S BODY POINTS UP THE ROAD AT THE LIGHT FOR ALL 18 SECONDS. His chest, his shoulders, his hips
and both of his feet face AWAY from the camera's starting position and up the road. THEY NEVER CHANGE
DIRECTION. He does not rotate, pivot, swivel or reposition his body at any point in this clip.

HIS FEET NEVER LEAVE THE GROUND. He takes no step in any direction. He is rooted where he stands.

WE GET HIS FACE ENTIRELY FROM THE CAMERA MOVING AROUND HIM. The camera curves forward and comes
around to his front. He does nothing to help it. He is not looking for the camera and he is not aware
of it.

MOTION STATE AT FRAME ONE

This clip BEGINS AT REST. At frame one the camera is locked and still. Danny is motionless, standing
on the dirt road behind the truck with both boots on the ground, one hand resting forward and down on
the top edge of the tailgate at chest height, both hands empty. Tyler is motionless far up the
road with his back turned and his head lifted. The corn is dead still. There is no wind. Nothing in
the frame is moving. The clip's job is to break that stillness.

IDENTITY SEPARATION

DANNY and TYLER are two completely different people and are never swapped, blended or substituted.
— DANNY is NEAR CAMERA, BARE-HEADED, standing on the road behind the truck, and cannot move.
— TYLER is FAR UP THE ROAD, wearing a CAP, back turned, and is the one being struck.
THE CAP IS THE TELL: capped figure = Tyler, bare-headed figure = Danny. This holds in every frame.
The near figure is never capped. The far figure is never bare-headed. They never trade places.

EXACTLY TWO PEOPLE EXIST IN THIS CLIP. No third person appears on the road, in the corn, near the
truck or at any frame edge.

GEO SPATIAL LAYOUT — LOCKED

— A straight dirt farm road between tall corn walls. The dead pickup sits on the road, its nose
  pointing UP THE ROAD toward the light, its tailgate toward the camera's starting position.
— DANNY stands ON THE DIRT ROAD, AT ROAD LEVEL, roughly THREE FEET BEHIND the truck's rear end,

— TYLER stands on the road roughly 80 FEET BEYOND DANNY, back turned, facing up the road. He is
  roughly 125 feet from the camera at the start — a small figure, about a seventh of the frame's
  height. He is a SHAPE, not a face.
— THE LIGHT hangs roughly 700 FEET up the road and roughly 250 FEET ABOVE it. Small, cold white,
  hard. IT NEVER MOVES, never approaches, never descends and never changes size.
— THE CAMERA starts BEHIND AND ABOVE the truck at roughly 11 FEET of height, looking straight up the
  road. It ends at roughly 7 FEET from Danny, at CHEST HEIGHT, ahead of him and off to one side,
  looking back at his face.
— NOTHING ELSE EXISTS. No second vehicle, no buildings, no poles, no signs, no animals, no debris.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING

Exactly the start image, unchanged. A wide, dark, backlit frame from behind and above the truck.

DANNY'S BACK, near camera and LOW IN THE FRAME, standing on the road at ground level behind the
truck. THE TRUCK BED'S TOP EDGE CUTS ACROSS HIM AT CHEST HEIGHT — his head and shoulders rise above
it, everything from his chest down is behind and below it, and his boots are hidden by the truck's
rear end. One hand reaches forward and down onto the top edge of the tailgate.

He is a black shape with a cold rim along the tops of his shoulders and the crown of his head. The
truck's flank runs away from him up the road. Tyler far up the road, small, centre frame, back
turned, head lifted. The light beyond him, small and cold, high above the road.

NO READABLE TEXT ANYWHERE IN FRAME.

FORMAT MODE

Cinematic widescreen, photorealistic 35mm. The film's own camera. Single continuous take, no cuts.
Not handheld, not found footage.

OPTICS

Moderate wide anamorphic prime, approximately 50 degrees diagonal field of view. FIXED focal length,
NO ZOOM: every change of size comes from the camera physically travelling.

Focus rides with the camera. At the start it is deep enough that both Danny's silhouette and Tyler's
distant figure are legible. As the camera closes on Danny it comes onto DANNY'S EYES and stays there,
and the corn and road behind him go progressively softer. Anamorphic horizontal flare off the light
while the light is in frame. Fine organic grain.

CAMERA — ONE CURVING MOVE, NEVER A PASS-AND-SWING-BACK

The camera is LOCKED and STILL for the first five seconds. It has not moved all night and it does not
move here.

At 0:05 it BREAKS. In one continuous ungraceful movement it DROPS from 11 feet of height down to
CHEST HEIGHT and begins TRAVELLING FORWARD up the road — and at the same time it begins CURVING TO
ITS OWN RIGHT, swinging out toward the right-hand edge of the road as it advances.

IT IS ONE SMOOTH CURVE ALL THE WAY AROUND HIM. The camera never runs past him and then swings back to
find him. It never whips. It never loses him. He is inside the frame continuously for the entire
move, and the world rotates behind him as the camera arcs.

WHAT THE ARC DOES TO THE FRAME — THIS IS THE POINT OF THE SHOT:
— DANNY starts as a BACK, near and low in frame. As the camera comes around he becomes a rimmed edge,
  then a three-quarter, then a near-frontal face.
— TYLER and THE LIGHT drift steadily toward FRAME RIGHT as the camera curves, and EXIT THE FRAME AT
  THE RIGHT EDGE around 0:10. After that they are never seen again in this clip.
— THE TRUCK'S FLANK sweeps across the frame during the arc and settles as a long dark mass behind
  Danny on FRAME LEFT.
— THE FRAME TIGHTENS FASTER AND FASTER as the camera closes, even though its speed never changes.
  That is perspective, not a speed ramp. DO NOT ADD A SPEED RAMP.

FRAMING PROGRESSION:
— 0:00 WIDE, HIGH, BACKLIT. Danny's back near and low. Tyler small, centre. The light beyond.
— 0:07 The camera is low and moving. Danny turning into a rimmed edge. Tyler drifting frame right.
— 0:10 Three-quarter on Danny, light at the right edge and going.
— 0:12 MEDIUM. Danny near-frontal, keyed. Truck a dark mass frame left. Right of frame is empty road
  and corn.
— 0:13 to end MEDIUM CLOSE-UP. Danny's head and shoulders, near-frontal three-quarter, slightly LEFT
  OF CENTRE. The camera arrives at roughly 7 feet and drifts almost to a stop, still barely moving on
  the final frame.

THE CAMERA NEVER PANS ON THE SPOT, never tilts, never zooms, never reframes and never reverses
direction. Its aim changes only as a consequence of the curve it is travelling on.

Once it is moving it carries the real judder of a camera travelling over uneven dirt — continuous fine
vibration, small vertical bumps over ruts. Never enough to read as handheld.

ACTION TIMING

0:00–0:02 — LOCKED
The start image, held, unchanged. Camera still. Danny's back, standing on the road behind the truck
at ground level, the bed's top edge crossing him at chest height, one hand reaching down onto the
tailgate. Tyler far up the road, back turned, head lifted. Total silence.

0:02–0:04 — PULSE ONE HITS TYLER
Up by the light, the corn FLATTENS in a wide travelling wave and a shove of air runs down the road.

TYLER IS STRUCK. His whole body is driven back a half step. His head snaps down and forward, his
shoulders collapse inward, and one knee dips before he catches himself. AND HE YELLS — a real man's
cry of pain, raw and human, unprocessed, cut short.

DANNY DOES NOT MOVE. Not a step, not a flinch of the feet. His hand tightens on the tailgate.

The camera has not moved.

0:04–0:05 — HE TRIES TO MOVE AND CANNOT
Danny's weight pitches forward. His upper body leans, one shoulder drives ahead of the other, his
hand comes off the tailgate — AND HIS FEET DO NOT LEAVE THE GROUND. Neither one lifts. The effort is
completely visible in his back and shoulders and it produces no travel at all.

His knees are locked and visibly trembling.

0:05–0:07 — PULSE TWO — HE BLOCKS AND IT DOESN'T HELP — AND THE CAMERA BREAKS
The corn flattens again up by the light.

TYLER THROWS BOTH ARMS UP IN FRONT OF HIS FACE AND HEAD — a clear, readable silhouette shape against
the light, elbows out, forearms crossed high. IT DOES NOT PROTECT HIM. He is driven back again,
harder than the first time, his arms buckling back against his own head, his body folding at the
waist, one knee going down to the dirt and coming back up. HE YELLS AGAIN, louder and more broken
than before.

ON THE SAME BEAT THE CAMERA BREAKS. It drops fast from 11 feet to chest height and starts travelling
forward and curving to its own right. The move is fast and slightly ungraceful — a camera being
snatched up and carried, not a smooth crane.

DANNY STILL DOES NOT MOVE HIS FEET.

0:07–0:11 — THE ARC
One continuous curving travel. The camera advances and swings around Danny at chest height.

Danny's body does not change direction. He stays pointed up the road. The camera comes around him:
back, to rimmed edge, to three-quarter.

Tyler and the light drift steadily toward FRAME RIGHT. Around 0:10 they pass the right edge of frame
and are gone. The truck's flank sweeps through frame and settles frame left.

AS THE LIGHT LEAVES THE FRAME, IT ARRIVES ON HIS FACE. The moment it passes behind the lens it
becomes a hard cold frontal key from upper frame right, and Danny's face is revealed. THE LIGHT ITSELF
HAS NOT CHANGED AT ALL — only the camera's position relative to it has.

Corn rows sweep past the frame edges close and fast with heavy motion blur. Dust hangs where the
pulses threw it.

0:11–0:13 — HIS FACE ARRIVES, AND IT IS ALREADY WRECKED
The camera settles at roughly 7 feet, near-frontal three-quarter, Danny slightly LEFT OF CENTRE.

THE FACE THE LIGHT FINDS HAS ALREADY COME APART, and the audience is only now allowed to see it. He
has been like this for eleven seconds in the dark:
— EYES WIDE with white showing clearly ABOVE the iris, wet, and flicking.
— INNER EYEBROW ENDS DRIVEN UP AND TOGETHER, hard, creasing the centre of his forehead into deep
  vertical folds. This is the single most important detail in the clip.
— JAW SLACK, mouth open, chin low. THROAT TENDONS standing out, a swallow that does not complete.
— BOTH HANDS SHAKING with a real visible tremor at the fingers and wrists, and it does not stop.

He is not looking at the camera. His eyes are past it and above it, up the road.

0:13–0:16 — PULSE THREE, OFF SCREEN, ON HIS FACE
OFF SCREEN AND BEHIND THE CAMERA: the wide dry roar of corn flattening far up the road. Then TYLER'S
YELL again — further away, weaker, more broken, and cut off sooner.

NONE OF IT IS VISIBLE. WE WATCH IT LAND ON DANNY'S FACE INSTEAD.

His eyes squeeze most of the way shut and open again. His head jerks a few degrees, an involuntary
tremor, not a performed refusal. His breath comes back BROKEN — a stuttering catching inhale in three
or four hitches instead of one smooth pull.

AND HE TRIES TO MOVE AGAIN. A real, full-body attempt: his torso pitches forward hard, both arms come
back for a running start, and ONE FOOT DRAGS AN INCH ACROSS THE DIRT AND STOPS. He does not go
anywhere. His body is trying and his legs will not answer.

0:16–0:18 — THE NEXT ONE IS COMING AND HE KNOWS IT
The rhythm has been steady enough that the audience is counting. The gap runs out.

Danny's face registers the approach with nothing but stillness and shaking. One thin involuntary sound
escapes high in his throat — not a word, not a scream, not a sob. His hands keep shaking. His feet do
not move.

END FRAME: his face, keyed hard and cold, mouth open, brows driven up and together, rooted where he
stands, with the camera still drifting almost imperceptibly. Nothing resolves.

NO OTHER ACTION OCCURS. Danny never runs, never steps, never falls, never speaks and never gets into
the truck. Tyler never chases anyone and never comes toward the camera.

PHYSICS

DANNY'S BODY POINTS UP THE ROAD FOR ALL 18 SECONDS. At 0:00, 0:05, 0:09, 0:13 and 0:17 his chest,
shoulders, hips and both feet point in the same direction — away from the camera's starting position
and up the road. His body does not rotate, pivot, twist or swivel at any point.

DANNY IS AT ROAD LEVEL FOR ALL 18 SECONDS. Both boots are on the dirt at 0:00, 0:05, 0:09, 0:13 and
0:17. He never climbs, steps up, mounts, stands on or is lifted onto any part of the truck. NO PART
OF HIM IS EVER ABOVE ROAD LEVEL.

DANNY'S FEET NEVER LEAVE THE GROUND. He takes no step forward, backward or sideways in all 18
seconds. The only foot movement in the clip is the ONE INCH OF DRAG at 0:14, which stops immediately.

REAL GROUND CONTACT: his boots are in loose dirt, the dirt is scuffed and disturbed around them where
he has been shifting his weight, and his shadow lies flat along the road surface at road level. When
his torso pitches forward on each attempt, the dirt under his boots grinds and does not release him.

THE PARALYSIS IS PHOTOGRAPHED AS EFFORT WITHOUT TRAVEL. The upper body pitches, the shoulders drive,
the arms come back, the neck strains, the chest heaves — and none of it produces any movement across
the ground. The knees stay locked and visibly tremble. This contradiction is the shot: a man throwing
everything he has into running and going nowhere.

THE TREMOR IS REAL AND SMALL. Hands shaking at the fingers and wrists, not the whole arm. Knees
trembling, not buckling. Head shaking a few degrees, not swinging. Adrenaline, not shivering.

THE PULSES HAVE PHYSICAL FORCE AND A LIMITED REACH. Each one sends a real blast of air outward from
the light. Near the light the corn FLATTENS completely in a travelling wave. Further down the road the
effect weakens with distance — bending, then rippling, then barely stirring. At Danny's position, 780
feet away, the air only lifts dust off the road and moves his clothing slightly.

THE BLAST IS AIR AND PRESSURE ONLY. It moves things by pushing them. NO visible shockwave, NO
expanding ring, NO distortion front, NO energy wave, NO glow, NO light effect travelling with it. The
only evidence a pulse happened is that things move.

TYLER TAKES REAL DAMAGE FROM EACH ONE. Real mass being driven backward: heels skidding in dirt, body
folding at the waist, a knee going down and coming back up, arms buckling against his own head. He
does not fly, does not tumble and is not thrown off his feet. He absorbs it and stays standing.

THE PULSES ARRIVE ON A SLOW STEADY RHYTHM — roughly every three seconds, four times across the clip.
The regularity is deliberate and must not be random.

THE CAMERA HAS REAL MASS. The drop is fast and slightly ungraceful; the travel carries continuous
judder and small bumps over ruts. It moves at one steady rate with no ramping and no easing.

THE TRUCK IS COMPLETELY INERT. It does not rock, settle, creak or move. No door moves.

LIGHTING

THE LIGHT UP THE ROAD IS THE ONLY SOURCE IN THIS CLIP. The truck is dead. There is no moon, no stars,
no ambient sky and no other light anywhere.

THE LIGHT'S OUTPUT IS ABSOLUTELY CONSTANT FOR ALL 18 SECONDS. It never brightens, dims, swells,
pulses, flickers or changes colour. EVERYTHING THAT CHANGES ABOUT THE LIGHTING IN THIS CLIP IS CAUSED
BY THE CAMERA MOVING, NOT BY THE LIGHT DOING ANYTHING.

FIRST HALF — BACKLIT (0:00 to about 0:10). The light is in front of the lens. Danny is a black shape
with a hard cold-white rim along the tops of his shoulders, the crown of his head and the outer edge
of his jaw. His face is in deep shadow and is NOT readable.

THE RIM COMES FROM THE LIGHT'S HEIGHT, NOT FROM HIS. The light hangs 250 feet ABOVE the road, so it
rakes DOWNWARD onto the tops of his shoulders and the crown of his head from far above. HE DOES NOT
NEED TO BE ELEVATED FOR THIS TO WORK AND HE IS NOT ELEVATED. He is standing on the dirt at road
level, partly overlapped by the truck, and the rim still lands because the source is above
everything. His head and shoulders read against the DARK ROAD SURFACE beyond the truck, not against
sky. Tyler is a pure black backlit silhouette
with a cold rim, and HIS CAP IS CLEARLY LEGIBLE IN THAT RIM. No facial detail on anyone.

THE HANDOVER (about 0:10). As the camera's curve carries the light past the right edge of frame, the
light passes BEHIND THE LENS. From that moment it falls directly onto Danny's face.

SECOND HALF — FRONT KEYED (0:10 to 0:18). A hard, cold, white key from UPPER FRAME RIGHT — a clean
edge on his forehead, brow, cheekbones, the bridge of his nose and his upper lip, with the underside
of his jaw and his throat in shadow.

HIS FACE IS THE BRIGHTEST THING IN THE FRAME AND IS FULLY READABLE for the last eight seconds. HE IS
NOT A SILHOUETTE IN THE SECOND HALF.

THE HARD KEY EXISTS TO SHOW HIS FACE FAILING. It rakes across the vertical folds between his brows,
catches the wet of his eyes, and picks up the tremor in his jaw and lower lip. Without a hard key none
of that survives.

THE LIGHT IS NEVER SHOWN AS A SOURCE ONCE IT LEAVES FRAME — no flare across the lens, no visible
shape, no glow at the frame edge. It is simply where the key comes from.

BRIGHTNESS IS CAPPED. While it is in frame the light is bright enough to rim bodies and never bright
enough to reveal anything around itself. NOTHING is ever visible around it — no craft, no hull, no
beam, no shaft, no cone, no rays, no outline, no structure.

THE TRUCK IS COMPLETELY DEAD. No headlights, no tail lights, no dash lights, no instrument glow, no
radio glow, NO DOME LIGHT despite the open doors. Its interior is TRUE BLACK.

THE CORN is barely separated from black. The road is faintly visible and no more. Everything the key
does not touch falls to TRUE BLACK.

DUST hangs in the air after each pulse, lit hard, drifting and settling slowly. Between pulses there
is no wind at all.

DIRT AND SWEAT on Danny: real, matte, dry road dust, streaked where sweat has run through it. Two or
three thin wet streaks at hairline and temples, no more. Because the key is hard, each streak catches
a bright specular line. NO drips, NO running beads, NO sheeting, NO glossy or oiled-looking skin.

BREATH: visible in the cold. Backlit and rimmed in the first half; caught hard by the key in the
second.

NOTHING FIERY OR RED ANYWHERE. Cold white only. THE SKY IS PURE BLACK — no stars, no moon, no cloud,
no horizon glow.

Colour: 85% true black, 10% cold blue-black, 5% hard cold white. No warm colour anywhere.

AUDIO

Total silence at frame one — no crickets, no wind, no engine, no room tone worth the name.

THE PULSES: each one a very low organic swell, subsonic, felt in the chest more than heard, arriving
on a SLOW STEADY RHYTHM roughly every three seconds. It is a rhythm, not a random event: the
regularity is the dread, and the audience should be counting toward the next one. NEVER a hum, drone,
engine tone, whine or synth. Closer to something enormous breathing.

With each pulse: the wide dry roar of corn flattening far up the road, then a much softer arrival of
air where Danny is.

TYLER'S CRIES: at 0:03 and again at 0:06, a REAL HUMAN MAN'S YELL OF PAIN. Raw, unprocessed, no
reverb tail beyond the flat slap off the corn walls, cut short each time. NOT a scream of terror, NOT
a growl, NOT a roar, NOT a shout of words, NOT anything inhuman or layered or pitched. It is a man
being hurt. The second is louder and more broken than the first.

At 0:14, a third cry from OFF SCREEN — further away, weaker, more broken, cut off sooner. Nothing is
visible when it happens.

DANNY: his breathing is the closest thing to the microphone and gets closer as the camera closes.
Fast, open-mouthed, ragged. It goes BROKEN at 0:14 — a stuttering catching inhale in three or four
hitches, then fast shallow gasps. And ONE THIN INVOLUNTARY SOUND high in his throat at 0:17 — not a
word, not a scream, not a sob, not a whimper of self-pity. Short. Bitten off.

DANNY'S BREATHING IS EXACTLY IN SYNC with his visible chest rise and fall throughout, with no drift
between the sound and the body.

Small sounds: his hand coming off the tailgate, his boot dragging an inch in the dirt at 0:14, his
clothing shifting.

NOBODY SPEAKS. Not one word from anyone. No music. No score. No subtitles. No sub-bass riser, no
rumble bed, no drone under the scene.

CHARACTER ACTING

DANNY IS THE SHOT. Everything else is happening to someone else.

HIS PERFORMANCE IS BUILT ON ONE CONTRADICTION: his body is trying as hard as it can to run and it is
not going anywhere. He is not choosing to stay. He is not being brave. He is not watching. HE IS
PARALYSED AND HE KNOWS IT, AND HE KEEPS TRYING ANYWAY.

Play the effort in the parts that CAN move — the pitch of the torso, the drive of the shoulders, the
arms coming back, the strain in the neck, the chest heaving. Play the failure in the legs: locked
knees, trembling, feet welded to the dirt. THE HARDER HE TRIES, THE MORE OBVIOUS THE FAILURE.

HE MAKES THREE ATTEMPTS AND EACH ONE IS BIGGER AND MORE DESPERATE THAN THE LAST — at 0:04, again
faintly at 0:09, and hardest at 0:14. None of them produces a step.

THE FACE, once the light finds it at 0:11, is ALREADY at full collapse — the audience is not watching
it happen, they are discovering it has already happened in the dark. Eyes wide with white above the
iris. INNER BROWS DRIVEN UP AND TOGETHER into deep vertical folds — that inner-brow lift is the
difference between exertion and terror and it must be there for the whole second half. Jaw slack,
mouth open, chin low. Throat working.

EVERY FEAR SIGNAL IS INVOLUNTARY. Tremor, blink rate, broken breath, jaw shake, throat sound. He is
not performing fear, he is leaking it. Nothing is chosen, nothing is theatrical, and none of it is
aimed at anyone.

⚠ HE DOES NOT SOB, SCREAM, WAIL, HYPERVENTILATE, CLUTCH HIS FACE, COLLAPSE, RAISE HIS HANDS
DEFENSIVELY OR SHAKE HIS HEAD DELIBERATELY. The fear is in tremor, breath, brow and jaw — not in
volume and not in gesture. Loud fear reads as acting; leaking fear reads as real.

HE NEVER LOOKS AT THE CAMERA AND NEVER MAKES EYE CONTACT WITH THE LENS. His eyes are aimed at a
physical point roughly forty feet ABOVE the road and seven hundred feet up it — past the lens and
above it in the second half. He does not know the camera is there.

TYLER IS A SHAPE, SO IT IS ALL IN SILHOUETTE. He is far away and backlit and there is no face to
work with. His whole performance is body outline against light:
— HIT ONE: driven back a half step, head snapping down, shoulders collapsing inward, one knee dipping.
— HIT TWO: BOTH ARMS UP HIGH IN FRONT OF HIS HEAD, elbows out, forearms crossed — a clear, blocky,
  instantly readable shape — and then that shape being crushed back against his own head as he folds
  at the waist and a knee goes to the dirt.
HE NEVER RECOVERS FULLY BETWEEN HITS. He is more bent after the second than after the first.

TYLER'S BACK IS TO CAMERA THE WHOLE TIME HE IS VISIBLE. He never comes toward the camera, never
chases anyone, and no facial detail is ever rendered on him.

NEITHER MAN LOOKS AT THE CAMERA AT ANY POINT.

STYLE

THE CAB CONTAINS NO WEAPON, NO TOOL, NO GUN, NO KNIFE, NO BAT, NO TIRE IRON AND NO USABLE OBJECT.
Every place he checks is empty.

AT 0:14 HIS EYELINE CHANGES to a nearer point and holds. He is no longer looking where the walking
figure was.

HE ENDS WITH BOTH HANDS OPEN AND EMPTY ON THE STEERING WHEEL, palms up, motionless.

THE TRUCK IS COMPLETELY DEAD. No headlights, no tail lights, no dash lights, no instrument glow, no
dome light, no radio. The engine never turns over and he never touches the ignition.

THE PULSES ROCK THE TRUCK AND STREAK THE GLASS WITH DUST. The dust stays on the glass and never
clears.

THE BLAST IS AIR AND PRESSURE ONLY. NO visible shockwave, NO expanding ring, NO distortion front, NO
energy wave, NO glow and NO light effect travelling with it.

BETWEEN PULSES THE AIR IS COMPLETELY DEAD. No ambient wind at any point.

NOTHING IS EVER VISIBLE AROUND THE REFLECTED LIGHT — no craft, no hull, no beam, no shaft, no cone,
no rays, no outline.

NOTHING FIERY OR RED APPEARS ANYWHERE. Cold white only.

THE SKY IN THE REFLECTION IS COMPLETELY BLACK — no stars, no moon, no cloud, no horizon glow.

HE NEVER LOOKS AT THE CAMERA.

The clip ends on the locked frame: a lit face behind dirty glass, both hands open on the wheel, a
smeared handprint in the dust, and a small standing shape reflected above his head with its head
lifted toward a light.


TAKE CHECKS — IN THIS ORDER

1. Is there EXACTLY ONE person in frame for all 18 seconds? Any second figure rendered as an actual
   body — at a window, beside the truck, in the cab — reject immediately.
2. IS HIS FACE ACTUALLY LIT AND READABLE through the glass? This is the entire point of the new
   camera position. If he's a silhouette, the shot has failed and the fix is more key on the face,
   not less dirt on the glass.
3. Is the REFLECTION present, dim, soft, and in the UPPER glass — and does it stay off his eyes?
4. Does the camera stay DEAD STILL while the TRUCK rocks? If the whole frame shakes, the camera got
   attached to the vehicle — reject.
5. Does he shout exactly ONE word, once, and never again?
6. After the shout, does he go STILL — with the inner brow pulling up and together — rather than
   sobbing or screaming? Screaming = reject; the stillness is the beat.
7. Does his face visibly CHANGE CHARACTER at 0:09 — grief out, function in?
8. Does he search behind the seat, under the seat, and the glovebox, in that order, and come up
   empty every time?
9. Are his hands EMPTY in the final frame, open on the wheel?
10. Does he stay in the cab the whole time — never opening a door, never getting out?
11. Is the mirror BARE — no rosary, no hanging object of any kind?
12. Is the truck completely dead — no dash glow, no dome light, no headlights?
13. Does the dust STAY on the glass after each pulse?
14. Any blood, wound or graphic detail in the reflection? Reject.
15. Does he ever look at the lens? Reject.


IF IT FAILS

HIS FACE IS TOO DARK — the likeliest failure, because the model knows this sequence as silhouettes.
Add to LIGHTING: "Danny's face is the brightest object in the frame. It is a full, clean, hard key
light on his features — both eyes, both cheekbones and the mouth are fully readable. He is NOT a
silhouette in this shot and must never be rendered as one."

THE REFLECTION SWALLOWS HIM — add to THE WINDSHIELD: "The reflection is no more than a quarter of
the brightness of his face and occupies only the top quarter of the glass."

THE REFLECTION DOESN'T APPEAR AT ALL — some models will render clean glass. Add: "The windshield is
strongly reflective in its upper portion, showing a clear mirrored image of the road, the light and
the figures behind the camera, laid over the view into the cab."

THE CAMERA SHAKES WITH THE TRUCK — add to CAMERA: "The camera is bolted to the ground and is not
touching the vehicle. During the pulses the horizon line and the frame edges do not move by a single
pixel; only the truck moves within the frame."
